OKHWB v3 · chiral hue walks

48 vivid anchors + 960 hue-walk samples + 16 shared grays = 1,024 unique colors. Each triangle makes one continuous walk toward the next source hue. Only the vivid tip keeps its exact source hue; the other twenty cells advance evenly along the walk.

Three walks, each with its mirror

The freehand sketches become an inward spiral, a column snake, and an outer edge followed by folded columns. Each visits all 21 colored cells once, moving between neighboring lattice points. Swapping white and black gives its opposite chirality while preserving the vivid starting tip.

Follow the numbers from 0 to 20. Every step adds 7.5° / 21 ≈ 0.357143°. The final sample reaches +7.142857°; the next source hue is one more step away. Each pattern appears eight times across the 48 triangles.

Exact construction and measured distances

Source hue H₀ = sector × 7.5°, for sectors 0–47. Use the same W = i/6 and B = j/6 lattice as v1, with nonnegative integers i + j < 6. For a cell’s traversal rank r, H = (H₀ + r × 7.5° / 21) modulo 360. Rank zero always has W = B = 0. Mirroring swaps W and B in the path; both chiralities advance hue in the same direction.

The repeating order is spiral, mirrored spiral, column snake, mirrored column snake, edge and folds, mirrored edge and folds. The JSON records every path and sample. No additional traversal families are included.

The conversion uses Ottosson’s OKHWB definition: OKHSV V = 1 − B and S = 1 − W/(1 − B), with black handled explicitly. Reference sRGB conversion, then nearest-byte rounding.

This experiment changes hue allocation while keeping every W/B coordinate. It does not add intermediate tonal levels or enforce a minimum perceptual distance. No fitting, pruning, or fillers are applied.

Polygons indicate coordinate regions. The numbered lines connect cell interiors to show traversal order; their lengths and cell areas do not represent perceptual distances or gamut volumes.
